findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy Header
findings.description: The HTTP response does not include the 'Content-Security-Policy' security header. CSP restricts which resources the browser is permitted to load, mitigating XSS and data injection attacks.
findings.remediation: Add a Content-Security-Policy header to your web server or application. Start with a strict policy such as: "default-src 'self'" and loosen only as needed. Refer to https://content-security-policy.com for guidance.

findings.title: Sensitive Path Accessible: Admin Panel
findings.description: The path '/admin' responded with HTTP 200. Administrative interface exposed publicly.
findings.remediation: Restrict or remove access to '/admin'. Ensure sensitive files and directories are not served by the web server. For directory listings: set 'Options -Indexes' in Apache or 'autoindex off;' in nginx. Remove .git, .env, and backup files from web-accessible directories.

findings.title: Sensitive Path Accessible: Robots.txt
findings.description: The path '/robots.txt' responded with HTTP 200. robots.txt may reveal hidden paths and admin endpoints.
findings.evidence_raw:
=== REQUEST ===
GET http://127.0.0.1:5000/robots.txt
User-Agent: SentinelScan/1.0 (security-research; authorized-scan)
Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, zstd
Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,*/*;q=0.8
Connection: keep-alive
Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.5
Cookie: lab_session=demo-session-token-12345


=== RESPONSE ===
Status: 200
Server: Werkzeug/3.1.9 Python/3.14.10
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:33:19 GMT
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 70
Connection: close

Response excerpt:
User-agent: *
Disallow: /admin
Disallow: /internal/
Disallow: /backup


=== NOTES ===
Path: /robots.txt
HTTP status: 200
Reason: robots.txt may reveal hidden paths and admin endpoints
findings.remediation: Restrict or remove access to '/robots.txt'. Ensure sensitive files and directories are not served by the web server. For directory listings: set 'Options -Indexes' in Apache or 'autoindex off;' in nginx. Remove .git, .env, and backup files from web-accessible directories.

findings.title: Missing X-Frame-Options Header
findings.description: The HTTP response does not include the 'X-Frame-Options' security header. This header prevents the page from being embedded in an iframe, defending against clickjacking attacks.
findings.remediation: Add: X-Frame-Options: DENY or X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN to prevent framing by malicious sites.

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options Header
findings.description: The HTTP response does not include the 'X-Content-Type-Options' security header. Setting this to 'nosniff' stops browsers from MIME-sniffing responses away from the declared content type.
findings.remediation: Add: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff to all responses.

findings.title: Cookie 'lab_session' Missing HttpOnly Flag
findings.description: The cookie 'lab_session' does not carry the HttpOnly flag. Without this flag, client-side JavaScript can read the cookie, making it vulnerable to theft via cross-site scripting (XSS).
findings.remediation: Add the HttpOnly attribute to the 'lab_session' cookie. Example: Set-Cookie: session=value; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict

findings.title: Technology Banner Disclosed via Server
findings.description: The response header 'Server' reveals backend technology details: 'Werkzeug/3.1.9 Python/3.14.10, Werkzeug/3.0.1 Python/3.11'. A specific version number is disclosed, which helps attackers quickly look up known vulnerabilities (CVEs) for that version.
findings.remediation: Remove or suppress the 'Server' header in your web server or application configuration. For nginx: 'server_tokens off;'  For Apache: 'ServerTokens Prod' and 'ServerSignature Off'  For Express.js: 'app.disable("x-powered-by");'

findings.title: Technology Banner Disclosed via X-Powered-By
findings.description: The response header 'X-Powered-By' reveals backend technology details: 'Flask/3.0.3 Python/3.11'. A specific version number is disclosed, which helps attackers quickly look up known vulnerabilities (CVEs) for that version.
findings.remediation: Remove or suppress the 'X-Powered-By' header in your web server or application configuration. For nginx: 'server_tokens off;'  For Apache: 'ServerTokens Prod' and 'ServerSignature Off'  For Express.js: 'app.disable("x-powered-by");'

findings.title: Missing Referrer-Policy Header
findings.description: The HTTP response does not include the 'Referrer-Policy' security header. Controls how much referrer information is sent with requests, reducing information leakage to third parties.
findings.remediation: Add: Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or a stricter value) to control referrer leakage.

findings.title: Missing Permissions-Policy Header
findings.description: The HTTP response does not include the 'Permissions-Policy' security header. Restricts which browser features (camera, microphone, etc.) the page and embedded iframes may use.
findings.remediation: Add a Permissions-Policy header listing only the features your application actually uses. Example: Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()

findings.title: Cookie 'lab_session' Missing SameSite Attribute
findings.description: The cookie 'lab_session' has no SameSite attribute. Without SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax, the browser will send this cookie with cross-site requests, increasing CSRF risk.
findings.remediation: Add SameSite=Strict (or SameSite=Lax) to the 'lab_session' cookie. SameSite=Strict provides the strongest protection; use Lax if top-level navigations must carry the cookie.
